title: An event bus that is safe to iterate

blocks.text: Listeners are read on every event and changed rarely: the page's case for `CopyOnWriteArrayList`. Every write copies the array, and every iteration walks a **snapshot**, so a listener may subscribe or unsubscribe while an event is being delivered, with no `ConcurrentModificationException` and no lock. The page also warns that `Collections.unmodifiableList` is only a read-only **view**: the list behind it can still change. `List.copyOf` is a real copy.
Write `EventBus`, where a listener is a `Consumer<String>`:

items: `subscribe(listener)` and `unsubscribe(listener)` (which returns whether it was subscribed) change the listeners.

`fire(event)` calls every listener subscribed when the delivery **starts**, in subscription order. A listener may subscribe or unsubscribe listeners, itself included, from inside its call: the current delivery goes on over the listeners it started with.
`listeners()` returns the current listeners as an unmodifiable copy that never changes afterwards.

rows: C does not get `"e1"`, and gets `"e2"`

cases.says: fire(event) calls every subscribed listener in subscription order, and unsubscribe stops a listener's deliveries.
A listener that unsubscribes itself while an event is being delivered causes no error, and the other listeners still get the event.
A listener subscribed while an event is being delivered does not get that event, only later ones: delivery iterates a snapshot.
listeners() returns an unmodifiable copy that does not change when listeners are added later, unlike a read-only view.

concepts: CopyOnWriteArrayList iterates a snapshot, so listeners can change during delivery without ConcurrentModificationException.
Collections.unmodifiableList is only a read-only view of a list that can still change; List.copyOf is a real copy.
